verdict.rationale: Working Copy documents its own secure credential storage: an in-app Identity holds an imported or generated private key, and SSH keys can live in the Secure Enclave behind Face ID or Touch ID. The docs do not explicitly say that one stored credential is reused across multiple hosts or repositories. Automatic public-key registration with GitHub and BitBucket hints at this but does not confirm it. Missing for 10: explicit documentation of one credential referenced across multiple hosts, coverage of non-SSH credentials (https tokens/passwords) in the vault, independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a developer, I can store credentials once in a secure vault and reference them from multiple hosts

citations.quote: You attach a private key to your Identity which can be imported or generated inside the app.
For extra security SSH keys can reside on the Secure Enclave protected by Face ID or Touch ID.
If you tap "Connect with BitBucket" or "Connect with GitHub" your public key will automatically be registered with BitBucket or GitHub.
